newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends firmer, but well off highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends firmer, but well off highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended mainly firmer, but well off new contract highs set early in the day, after a round of profit-taking cut into gains, traders said.

Options-linked selling ahead of the March options expiry today, as well as steady rollover of spot March into second-month May also put a damper on the market's rally, traders said. March enters delivery period February 20.
"There was steady options-related selling above 150.00 (cents a lb basis March)," one trader said. "And funds rolling March into May."

March delivery ended up 0.25 cent, to 151.25 cents, after jumping a fresh life-of-contract high of 154.75 cents. The low was 148.40. May finished 1.20 cents higher, at 146.00 cents, while the back months closed unchanged to up 2.50 cents.

The market headed higher at the outset, as operators followed through on Thursday's strong rally. Buying accelerated after Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation announced the country's production fell to 778,000 60-kg bags in January compared to 2.08 million 60-kg bags in January 1996.

But a federation source said that the figure appeared worse than it really was when compared to abnormally high production figures in the same month last year. He said the average January output is about 800,000 60-kg bags.

However, Hencorp Becstone president Victor Henriquez said the Colombia news was bullish. He said the January output could point to a smaller 1996/97 Colombian crop compared with preliminary estimates of around 12.5 million 60-kg bags.
Technically, traders said March's difficulty getting past resistance at 155.00 cents may have prompted operator to take profits, but the charts continued to look friendly.
"Technically, the market looks terrific," Henriquez said. "The uptrend is intact. Just close your eyes and buy the dips."
Volume Friday was heavy, at an estimated 16,645 lots.
